subject: maths
question: Two similar triangles, Triangle X and Triangle Y, have perimeters of 24 cm and 36 cm, respectively. If the area of Triangle X is 40 cm², what is the area of Triangle Y?
solution:
&
lt;p>**Given:**

Perimeter of Triangle X = 24 cm

Perimeter of Triangle Y = 36 cm

Area of Triangle X = 40 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Ratio of perimeters of similar triangles = Ratio of corresponding sides

Ratio of areas of similar triangles = Square of ratio of corresponding sides

**Calculation:**

⇒ Ratio of sides = 36 ÷ 24

⇒ Ratio of sides = 3 ÷ 2

⇒ Ratio of areas = (3 ÷ 2)²

⇒ Ratio of areas = 9 ÷ 4

⇒ Area of Triangle Y = 40 × 9 ÷ 4

⇒ Area of Triangle Y = 40 × 2.25

⇒ Area of Triangle Y = 90 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 90 cm².**
